scope: Committed generation alarms through an opt-in owned timer and private system commands, preserving ordinary leader/current-term admission, private execution, LTX commitment/publication and durability proofs. Reserved per-history internal command identity, explicit limits, pre-catalog capability/capacity refusal and joined domain cancellation. Outbox delivery remains unimplemented.
environment: macOS native Rust Node/SDK/SQLite/LTX/Raft Engine/TLS and conditional in-memory object stores. Alarm behavior uses three actual voters; the disabled/capacity preflight creates one Node with explicit development-voter configuration but no Raft engine/group or catalog object. No cellar_internal_tests.
limitations: Component qualification only. All 322 unique Rust cases across 19 binaries and all31 checks pass at this source; 9 child entry points execute through owning parents and are excluded. Eight native effects cases include the prior three Blob cases and five new alarm cases. After arming a five-second alarm and reading its committed predecessor on all voters, the primary is stopped, followed by an eight-second interval with no incoming business/status/admin calls. The first audit finds exactly one callback on a surviving leader and value7 on both survivors. A held private callback cannot schedule its unpublished alarm; release commits then produces one firing and value9 on all voters. Rearm/cancel suppress old generations; a normal caller with the correct system-operation digest is refused without consuming the business sequence. Four preflight variants (disabled scheduler,one-byte input capacity,one client identity,one retained receipt) create no Raft directory or S3 object and invoke no callback. Direct public Node shutdown returns within15seconds, joins its active timer domain and leaves retained Raft handles closed; the existing Fleet outcome does not supply a graceful Raft close receipt/archive obligations. MR-13 retains that semantic contract. New alarm cases use Quorum intents; S3 alarm-specific outage/failover cuts are not claimed. Existing S3 output/archive/restore tests retain their own boundary. Current Node regression is its affected exact Raft lifecycle case; the prior8cfc4bd Blob record separately retains all88 Node cases. Class capability/system contracts enter schema identity, while definitions without features preserve their prior identity. Callback execution remains private/speculative until ordinary command proof succeeds; there is no external exactly-once promise. Metadata is precharged, one SQL scan stays owned, and slow assigned SQL work can delay that timer. Existing receipt limits apply, with no automatic pruning or unlimited-duration claim. Only two of six original MR-12 requirements are implemented: Blob closure and no-traffic alarms. Outbox dispatch, durable destination receipts, leadership races, delivery progress, the full unsupported binding gate and examples remain required. MR-12 stays IN_PROGRESS; MR-13 through MR-17 remain open. No physical S3,power-loss,real failure-zone,production latency/capacity,24-hour soak,larger physical tier,federation or complete release is claimed. Existing vendored warnings remain visible.
